title: Potato Poker - lessons learned as a game designer that cannot code
author: Brilliant_Feed4158
selftext:
I am about to release Potato Poker, the final build is being reviewed by Steam. If you like the concept [wishlist the game on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5503910/) or download the [demo on itch.io](https://potatopoker.itch.io/potato-poker-demo).

For a long time I have been developing and designing games. Just for fun as side projects. There was always some game idea I wanted to explore. Some time ago I kept hearing how good the LLMs can code, so I decided to try myself. *This has definitely not been a "one prompt" game!*

I have worked with a developer before, so I had some experience in explaining someone (or in this case some thing) what I wanted. With the developer I was very careful: "could you maybe add this? Nice feature, but maybe a little bit more like so?" because I knew anything I would ask was a lot of work! -- Not with the LLM. Here I could go all out and tweak things until they where exactly what I wanted. This allowed me to go all out on all kinds of details, extra's and fun secret things. Some things that some users will not even discover!

The idea for the game: *what if you can buy upgrades in Texas Hold'em and so slightly increase chances of recieving a good card in your hole cards? Or a flop with increased chances for suited cards. Not automatically always a good card, but an increased chance. And the better the upgrades, the higher the chance.*

I wanted the game to give a feel of being on the road, an adventure, with the atmosphere of Governor of Poker.

**Blueprint**

Although I am not a coder, I do have some project management experience. A couple things I did first:  
1) have a chat with ChatGPT on the platform that I wanted to build on and publish and all aspects around the game.  
2) I then explained as detailed as possible alle the game mechanisms, the world, the style, the story, AI playstyle, the general atmosphere - anything I could think of.

This led to a blueprint with a quite comprehensive description of the game. This is really important, because it's harder to make fundamental changes later in the project.

**Building the project**  
  
Before any code could be written, the LLM had to guide me through Godot. Then connected the LLM to the project. I first asked it to make a vertical slice and get the poker running. In a couple days I had the backbone of the game running. 

From then on I just started adding features. This was quite addicting! In a train ride I would get *so much done* that I really wanted to build any free moment! 

Poker AI of the opponents took one day. I really wanted a variety in styles and skill. So it did take me more testing, tweaking, testing, tweaking. But again I was flabbergasted just how quick it build the AI.

**UI and other assets**

For the UI and other assets I often just used paint to make extremely simple mockups that showed where in the screen I wanted things and their shape. What really helped me is to provide a mockup and then ask for 3 concepts. Iterate further on the concept you like. 

What really helps is if you know the language of photoshop: "feather the edge", "add a bevel", stuff like that.

**Audio**

I probably could have took a better, more automated approach, but audio was quite hard actually! Describing what a sounds sounds like is really hard! And even if I used an LLM for prompting, I rarely got the sound I hoped for. This required A LOT of retries.

**Steam - the many hoops you have to jump through**

Working on the game was really fun. Getting it on Steam was a pain in the ass! Without an LLM to guide me on almost every step along the way, I would simply not have been able to do it. So many options stuffed away, no idea what they're doing or why it's on or off. 

**Costs**

\- Steam game: $100   
\- 2 months Pro subscription OpenAI $200  
\- Elevenlabs $20

**Time:**  
2 months. Every available hour outside of work, kids, social stuff I would work on it. 

If you like the concept [wishlist the game on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5503910/) or download the [demo on itch.io](https://potatopoker.itch.io/potato-poker-demo).
